title: Kentucky Kingdom to open world's largest indoor wooden coaster
summary:
Kentucky Kingdom in Louisville is set to open the world's largest indoor wooden roller coaster as part of a multi-year investment programme by operator Herschend.

Named Midnight Showdown, the family-friendly, horse-racing-themed wooden roller coaster is due to open in spring 2027.

It will be Kentucky Kingdom's seventh roller coaster, giving the park the highest coaster count of any theme park in Kentucky.

The attraction will serve as the centrepiece of Bluegrass Downs, a new land inspired by Kentucky’s horse-racing heritage.

Bluegrass Downs brings Kentucky's horse-racing heritage to life through new theming and reimagined rides at Kentucky KingdomKentucky Kingdom

Standing more than three storeys tall, the ride will feature 1,130 feet of wooden track and two trains, each seating 10 riders.

The indoor coaster will combine 11 airtime moments with twists and turns, while lighting, audio and visual effects will recreate the atmosphere of a night-time horse race.

Bluegrass Downs will also see five existing rides reimagined to fit the new theme. The former Mad Hatter will become Jolly Juleps, a spinning teacup ride, while the Musical Carousel will become My Old Kentucky Carousel, retaining its musical instrument-themed vehicles.

The former Zeppelin ride will become Soaring Silks, while Scream Extreme will be rethemed as Whirlwind. Bumper Cars will become Bumper Derby, featuring horse-themed vehicles.

Kentucky Kingdom's My Old Kentucky Carousel will receive new horse-racing-inspired theming as part of Bluegrass DownsKentucky Kingdom

Happy Valley Farm, a new themed land featuring eight reimagined rides, will also open in spring 2027, with eight rethemed rides, including Friendly Frogs, Loopy Lambs and Country Cruiser.

The area will also be home to Flying Fox, the park's suspended family coaster, which debuted in May 2026.

"We've been building toward this for years, and 2027 is the moment guests will see just how far Kentucky Kingdom has come,” said Carly Uglow, director of sales and marketing at Kentucky Kingdom.

She continued: "From two brand-new roller coasters and reimagined lands to refreshed rides and new theming throughout the park, this is a very different Kentucky Kingdom than guests may remember from years past."

title: Universal to add new indoor thrill coaster at Epic Universe
summary:
Universal Orlando Resort has announced a new indoor thrill coaster coming to Epic Universe.

Construction is already underway on the new coaster, which will be built in the park's Dark Universe land, next to Monsters Unchained: The Frankenstein Experiment.

Per a press release, the upcoming attraction at Epic Universe will immerse guests in a new story inspired by the Universal Monsters franchise.

Construction is underway on a new indoor thrill coaster for Dark Universe at Universal Epic UniverseUniversal

Details about the new indoor coaster, including its name and opening date, have yet to be announced. Universal said the attraction is planned to open in the "years ahead".

This comes as Universal Orlando Resort continues to expand its line-up of attractions and entertainment across the destination, with several new experiences planned over the coming years.

Universal Studios Florida will open a reimagined Universal Horror Make-Up Show featuring Blumhouse later this year. The park will also welcome Fast & Furious: Hollywood Drift, a high-speed roller coaster, in 2027.

The new Universal Epic Universe coaster will be located next to Monsters Unchained: The Frankenstein Experiment.Universal

Other additions include a new signature full-service restaurant in the Jurassic Park area of Universal Islands of Adventure, opening in 2027, and Luke Combs’ Category 10, a new music and entertainment venue set to open at Universal CityWalk in late 2027.

In other Universal news, Epic Universe has integrated a new floating solar system as part of Universal Orlando Resort's renewable energy programme.

The 1.4 MW installation, developed by Qcells and D3Energy, was energised earlier this year and is now operational.

Dark Universe at Epic Universe, home to Frankenstein Manor and Monsters Unchained, is expanding its attractions line-up Universal

It forms part of three on-site solar installations at the theme park, which together have a capacity of 3.7 MW.

Together, the installations are forecast to generate more than 6.7 million kilowatt-hours of electricity each year, equivalent to the energy needs of more than 900 homes.

The floating array also supports the park's electric transport network. Solar energy is stored in batteries during daylight hours and used to charge Universal's electric buses overnight.
